items.action: Bind [(railOpen)] on ds-app-layout to a control that stays visible below 1024px, such as a menu button in the topbar, so the rail can be opened on a narrow screen.
items.appliesWhen: Every ds-app-layout at a viewport narrower than 1024px (the lg breakpoint, a compile-time media query). At 1024px and wider the rail is unchanged and railOpen has no effect.
items.pitfall: Nothing fails to build and a desktop check looks unchanged: the navigation disappears only on a narrow window or a phone, where an app with no railOpen toggle leaves its user without a way to reach it.
items.verify: At a window 900px wide the rail is off screen, a visible control opens it, and the scrim or Escape closes it again.

items.action: Add `@use '@ids-group-ltd/ids-design-system/styles/surface-motion';` to your styles entry, beside `styles/overlay-motion`. If you have no overlay-motion line, put it beside whatever DS partials you do `@use`. Order does not matter.
items.appliesWhen: Only à-la-carte consumers who `@use` DS partials individually. `styles/ds` forwards it, so its users need nothing at all.
items.pitfall: Missing it fails SILENTLY — no error, no warning. The keyframes simply do not exist, and modal, drawer, bottom-sheet, toast, banner, alert, loading-overlay and the overlay panels all render with no entrance animation. Write the package-qualified specifier too: a bare `styles/…` does not resolve in a consumer build.
items.note: A new global partial `styles/_surface-motion.scss` holds the shared entrance keyframes — ds-fade-in, ds-scale-in, ds-slide-in, ds-slide-edge-in — that every DS surface names through `--ds-<surface>-enter-keyframes`.

items.action: Gate on `sortDir`, not on `sortKey`. `if (sortKey())` becomes `if (sortDir())`, and a server query built as `orderBy: sortKey()` must skip the clause when `sortDir()` is null.
items.appliesWhen: Hosts that already read both need nothing, and neither do those passing `sortingOrder: ['asc','desc']`, which has no unsorted state. The table's own icons, aria-sort and client-side sorting were always gated on `sortDir` and still are.
items.pitfall: This item finds NOTHING in a template. The code that breaks is the host's own — a store, a page class, a query builder — and it names no DS symbol at all, so a search for `ds-table` comes back clean and the item gets recorded not-applicable. A common shape is `sorting: store.sortKey() ? { path: store.sortKey()!, order: store.sortDir() ?? 'Asc' } : undefined`, which keeps ordering a server-paged list by the last column the reader touched while the header shows no sort. Grep the `.ts` for the `detect` shapes.
items.note: `sortKey` is no longer nulled when the cycle reaches unsorted: it keeps naming the column the user last touched, and `sortDir === null` alone means unsorted. It fixes a header desync for hosts that map "off" back to their own default sort.
items.verify: No host builds a sort clause from the key alone: every place that turns (sortChange) into a query gates on the DIRECTION (`sortDir`), and a store that keeps both nulls the clause when the direction is null.

items.action: A form that validates and must not reflow turns it back on: `provideDsConfig({ field: { reserveMessage: true } })` app-wide, or `[reserveMessage]="true"` per field. Bindings you wrote as `[reserveMessage]="false"` to opt out can be deleted.
items.appliesWhen: All fourteen message-bearing fields: input, textarea, select, autocomplete, multi-select, checkbox, radio, radio-group, switch, slider, date-picker, time-picker, color-picker, otp-input.
items.pitfall: Two shifts, neither of which stops a build. A field with no hint gets about 23px shorter, so everything under it moves up — and then moves down again the first time a hint or error appears. And any tighter sub-stack you added to compensate for the old reserved gap now over-tightens: with the row collapsed, a normal 16px stack is correct again.
items.note: The default flipped from true to false and a config step was added: per-field input, then the new `DS_CONFIG.field.reserveMessage`, then false. At 0.7.0 the per-field input, defaulting to true, was the only source.
items.verify: Every surviving `[reserveMessage]="false"` sits under a `dsReserveMessages` host or an app config that turns the flag ON - anywhere else it restates the new default and does nothing.

items.action: None in the normal case. If you deliberately used a nested call to RESET a section to defaults, spell that section out: `provideDsConfig({ datePicker: { locale: 'en-US', dateFormat: undefined, firstDayOfWeek: 1 } })`.
items.appliesWhen: A single root-level `provideDsConfig` behaves exactly as before. Nested provision was neither documented nor safe to use.
items.note: A nested provider merges with the config above it section by section instead of replacing it wholesale — it used `useValue`, so a subtree setting one flag silently reset every unrelated section. The merge is what lets the new `dsReserveMessages` directive scope one field flag without disturbing the rest.
items.verify: No nested provideDsConfig relies on RESETTING a section it does not name - a nested call merges now, so a reset has to spell the section out.

items.action: Build right after upgrading — the compiler enumerates every collision. Per member: rename your own, or add `override` where the base semantics genuinely match.
items.appliesWhen: Only a consumer that EXTENDS a DS component class. Subclassing is unsupported (design-system.md § Components); anyone using the `<ds-…>` elements needs nothing.
items.pitfall: One change here is a REMOVAL, and it fails the other way round: TooltipDirective dropped its protected `onOpen`, split into `onPointerEnter` / `onFocusIn`, and `focusout` moved from `onClose` to a new `onFocusOut`. A subclass that overrode `onOpen` fails because its `override` now names a member the base does not declare — move the mouse-path body to `onPointerEnter` and the keyboard-path body to `onFocusIn`.
items.note: Additions: all fourteen message-bearing fields gained `reserveMessageResolved`; CheckboxComponent, SwitchComponent and RadioComponent a protected `devMode`; InputComponent and TextareaComponent `control` and `focus`; SearchComponent `focus`; TableComponent `rowId` and `rowKey`; PaginationComponent `showPageSize`; TimePickerComponent `label`, `required`, `optional`, `labelId`, `fullWidth`; DatePickerComponent `fullWidth`; AppLayoutComponent `railOpen`, `railLabel`, `compact`, `closeRail` and the private `navigation`, `destroyRef`, `watchDesktopBreakpoint`; TooltipDirective the protected `onPointerEnter`, `onFocusIn`, `onFocusOut` and the private `focusedTarget`, `describedElement`, `scheduleShow`. TooltipDirective lost `onOpen`, and LayoutScrollService gained `navigation` and lost `router`. TS4114 demands `override`, TS2415 fires on a redeclared private, TS2416 where a signature differs.
items.verify: A typecheck reports no TS4114 / TS2415 / TS2416 on any class extending a DS component; a subclass that overrode TooltipDirective.onOpen has moved its body to onPointerEnter / onFocusIn.

items.action: Only if a screen relied on the blanket reset: inject the still-public `LayoutScrollService` and call `scrollToTop()` from the handler that changes the filter.
items.appliesWhen: Nothing to do for anyone who found the old reset disruptive — that is the case this change serves.
items.note: The content scroll resets only when the PATH changes now, not on every NavigationEnd, so a sort, page or filter change that rewrites just the query string or fragment keeps the reader where they were.
items.verify: No screen depended on the blanket scroll reset: one that needs the top after a filter change calls LayoutScrollService.scrollToTop() from that handler.

items.action: Only if you set `flex`, `width` or `margin` on `.title` to control how the header row divides its space: move that declaration to `.heading`.
items.appliesWhen: Only a consumer who styles the modal internal DOM. Everyone else is untouched.
items.pitfall: `.title` is NOT renamed — it is still emitted, and a rule that only paints it (colour, font, letter-spacing) must NOT be re-pointed. Re-pointing it moves the paint onto a box that also wraps the eyebrow.
items.note: The `[eyebrow]` slot wrapped `<h2 class="title">` together with the eyebrow in a new `<div class="heading">`, and the `flex: 1` that used to sit on `.title` moved to that wrapper.
items.verify: Open a ds-modal-card that has both a title and an [eyebrow]: the title and eyebrow share one block that takes the free width, and the close button stays hard right. Any `.title` rule you kept still paints the heading text.

items.action: None for most tables — both changes are what a reader expects. Only if a screen deliberately relied on blanks sorting first, or on the old pure-lexical order of strings containing digits, supply a per-column `sortValue` that maps the values the way that screen wants.
items.appliesWhen: Both changes apply with or without the new per-column `sortValue`.
items.pitfall: Two orderings move at once and neither announces itself. Blanks used to be the smallest value, so on ascending they floated to the TOP; they sink to the bottom in both directions now. And the text fallback passes `{ numeric: true }` to localeCompare, so `item 9` precedes `item 10` instead of following it — a list that looked deliberately ordered can come back reordered.
items.note: A cell reads as no-data when it is an empty string or one of the em dash, en dash, hyphen, `n/a`, `never` or `none`, matched case-insensitively.
items.verify: No client-sorted screen depended on blanks sorting FIRST or on pure lexical order for strings with digits; where it did, a per-column sortValue says so.

informational: Purely additive, opt-in inputs — no consumer action: `ds-table` [rowId] accessor (row identity for tracking/selection/expansion; still defaults to row.id), `ds-date-picker`/`ds-time-picker` [fullWidth], `ds-pagination` [showPageSize], and public `focus(options?)` on `ds-search` / `ds-input` / `ds-textarea`.

`ds-table`'s row generic relaxes from `{ id: string }` to `object` so keyless data can supply [rowId]; rows that keep an `id` type-check exactly as before, and the resolver is public as `rowKey(row)`.

New override tokens, all defaulting to the current values: --ds-<surface>-enter-keyframes / -enter-duration / -enter-easing / -enter-scale across overlay panels, modal, drawer, bottom sheet, toast, banner, alert and loading overlay (-enter-offset on overlay, toast, banner, alert); -leave-duration / -leave-easing on modal, drawer, bottom sheet and toast; --ds-modal-eyebrow-* (5); --ds-modal-title-font-size; --ds-date-picker-trigger-radius; --ds-date-picker-panel-radius; --ds-checkbox-radius; --ds-popover-min-width; --ds-menu-min-width / -max-width; --ds-toast-min-width / -max-width; --ds-table-cell-pad-{top,right,bottom,left}; --ds-table-head-border-color / -weight / -tracking; --ds-pagination-label-font-size / -weight / -color.
`ds-modal` / `ds-modal-card` gained an `[eyebrow]` projection slot above the title; unfilled it renders nothing, so existing dialogs are unaffected.

`DS_CONFIG` gained a `field.reserveMessage` key — `provideDsConfig({ field: { reserveMessage: false } })` sets the message-row default for all 14 message-bearing fields. The per-field input still wins; its type widens to `boolean | null` (null = not set), so existing bindings and bare attributes behave identically.

Visual-only: overlay panels now enter FROM their trigger edge (a panel above its trigger rises instead of sliding down), a selected dropdown option keeps its tint under hover/keyboard-active, and a read-only `ds-modal` no longer draws an empty footer strip.
ds-time-picker gained label / required / optional inputs (additive) — a date + time form row now aligns without a hand-rolled label; existing usages without label render exactly as before.

Visual-only in ds-time-picker: the clock glyph moved from before the value to the trailing edge and grew 14px -> 16px, the value weight dropped from medium to regular, and the trigger gap narrowed 8px -> 4px, all to match ds-date-picker / ds-select / ds-input. Recover the old weight with --ds-time-picker-value-weight: var(--font-weight-medium).

Value typography of both pickers is now tokenised: --ds-date-picker-value-font-family / -font-size / -weight (mono default, shared with the ghost mask) and --ds-time-picker-value-font-family / -font-size / -weight, plus --ds-time-picker-required-color. Defaults unchanged except the time value weight noted above and, on both pickers, the value size at sm/lg, which now stays --font-size-s instead of following the size (xs/m).
ds-date-picker [fullWidth] now pushes the calendar glyph to the trailing edge instead of leaving it packed beside the value; only affects fields that opt into fullWidth.

`ds-app-layout` rail goes off-canvas below `lg` (1024px, a compile-time media query) for every consumer: it slides in only while the new two-way `[(railOpen)]` model is true, so a narrow screen needs a toggle bound to it; `railLabel` (default 'Navigation') names it for a screen reader. At/above `lg` nothing changes and `railOpen` has no effect. New tokens --ds-app-layout-rail-bg-color / -rail-shadow / --ds-app-layout-scrim-color all default to current values. The dialog role, aria-modal and focus trap read `--bp-lg` at runtime: without the emitted `--bp-*` scale they stay off (dev builds log a console.error), while the off-canvas CSS still applies. Include the DS global styles, or the bundled `styles/ds` entry, to get them.

`inheritDsConfig(config)` is a new public export beside `provideDsConfig`: it reads the nearest ancestor DS_CONFIG (skipSelf, optional) and shallow-merges per top-level section. Call it from an injection context if you need the merging behaviour in your own factory provider or directive metadata.

`dsReserveMessages` is a new directive: put it on a form and every DS field DECLARED inside reserves its message row, without a per-control binding. Presence-driven (no input), merges with the config above it, and a field's own [reserveMessage] still wins. Projected <ng-content> is not covered - it keeps the injector of the template it was written in.

Visual-only: dialogs opened through `ModalService` no longer carry the `ds-overlay-pane` panel class, so the shared overlay-panel entrance is no longer layered on top of the modal's own card/backdrop animation.

Known gap, not a regression: the ds-time-picker label wiring (aria-labelledby / aria-required) landed on the SINGLE-mode trigger only; range mode's start/end segment triggers are not wired to the label yet.

`TableColumn` gained an optional `sortValue: (row) => string | number | Date | null | undefined` so a column sorts by its domain value instead of the rendered text; formatted money, percents and dates sorted wrong before. Purely additive - a column without it keeps today's behaviour. Only affects sorting, not the header filter's value list.

`ds-checkbox`, `ds-switch` and `ds-radio` log a dev-mode warning when a caption is projected (`<ds-checkbox>text</ds-checkbox>`) instead of passed via [label]; the text never rendered and failed silently. All three share the [label]-only contract. Dev only - the detection node is gated on isDevMode(), so production is unchanged. Projection itself is still unsupported. The directive doing the detection is internal (not exported from public-api).

Known gap, not a regression: `--ds-overlay-enter-scale` is the one entrance token NOT forwarded onto a portaled overlay pane, so setting it per instance (`ds-select { --ds-overlay-enter-scale: 0.9 }`) has no effect on select / autocomplete / multi-select / date / time / colour picker / popover / tooltip / menu submenu panels. Scope it globally until it is forwarded; the other four (-enter-keyframes / -duration / -easing / -offset) do forward.

Bugfix, no action: `dsTooltip` now puts `aria-describedby` on the element that actually took focus (recorded from the bubbling `focusin`) rather than unconditionally on its host, so a tooltip on a host that is not itself focusable — `ds-menu-item` carries `role="none"` and holds the real button inside — finally reaches a screen reader. A pointer-only open still describes the host.

Visual-only fixes: `ds-pagination` pins its internal rows-per-page select to `reserveMessage: false` (it inherited the app default and pushed the pager off the page buttons' baseline), and `ds-stat`'s card fills a stretched host so a KPI row with mixed captions paints equal-height tiles. Consumers can drop the global workarounds for both (`ds-pagination ds-field-message { display: none }` and `ds-stat { height: 100% }`). (delete list: pagination-inner-select-hidden)

A selected dropdown option keeps its tint under hover and keyboard focus. The neutral hover/active branch out-ranked the selected one on specificity and repainted the row to --surface-secondary, and because the panel seeds the active state on the selected option when it opens, it showed at rest too rather than only under the cursor. The selected row now has its own hover/active step, --primary-muted. A brand override written against the old behaviour now stacks on top of the library step rather than replacing it. NO ACTION.

deleteList.why: The default is FALSE again, so an opt-out binding only restates it - unless the field sits under a `dsReserveMessages` host or an app config that turns it on, where the binding is still the way back out.
deleteList.replaceWith: nothing - delete the binding where no host reserves

deleteList.why: A tighter sub-stack or a negative margin added to swallow the reserved message row is now over-tightening a form that no longer reserves it.
A rule hiding the empty message row inside the pagination rows-per-page select. The component pins that select to its own compact shape now, so the row is gone at the source.
